title: Whoever repents and does good has truly turned to Allah.
subtitle: Repentance that is accepted, for any sin
then: Ibn Kathir says this shows {reward}His mercy extends to all His creatures{/reward}: whoever repents, He accepts it {reward}for any sin, great or small{/reward}. He links it to 4:110, 9:104 and 39:53, despair not of the mercy of Allah.
now: You have repented before and slipped again. You feel embarrassed to ask one more time. {idea}Turning back with good deeds is what makes it real{/idea}, and the door does not close because you came back again.
old: I have asked forgiveness too many times; it does not count anymore.
new: Every sincere turning back, followed by good, is accepted by Allah.
try: After asking forgiveness today, follow it with one specific good action within the hour.

title: They do not witness falsehood, and pass idle talk with dignity.
subtitle: Where the servants refuse to be present
then: Ibn Kathir says they do not bear witness to falsehood: {trap}lies, immorality, foul speech{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ warned against false speech and false testimony, {trap}repeating it until the Companions wished he would stop{/trap}. When they pass by idle talk, {idea}they do not let it touch them{/idea}.
now: The break-room conversation turns into mocking a colleague who is not there. You do not join in, but you stay and laugh. {idea}Being in the room is being a witness.{/idea} The servants find a way to leave with dignity.
old: I did not say anything bad, I was just there.
new: Where I choose to stay is part of what I testify to.
try: The next time a conversation turns to gossip or mockery, change the subject or walk away calmly.

title: Reminded of His verses, they do not fall deaf and blind.
subtitle: Letting the verses actually reach you
then: Ibn Kathir contrasts them with those who hear the words of Allah and {trap}are not moved to change their ways, as if deaf and blind{/trap}. The servants are like those in 8:2: {idea}when His verses are recited, their faith increases{/idea}.
now: The Quran plays in the car on the way to work while you answer messages at red lights. It is on, but you are not there. {idea}The servants let it in.{/idea} Even one verse heard properly can turn the day.
old: I listen to Quran a lot, so I am fine.
new: Hearing it is not enough. The servants let the verses change them.
try: Listen to one short surah today with nothing else in your hands, and notice one thing it asks of you.

title: Our Lord, give us spouses and children who cool our eyes.
subtitle: A dua for family and for leading in good

key.label: What comfort of the eyes is

then: Ibn Abbas said it means {reward}offspring who strive to obey Allah and bring joy in this world and the next{/reward}. Al-Miqdad said believers who saw loved ones refuse faith could not rest, and this dua was for that. Asking to be leaders means {idea}examples in good{/idea}, so guidance reaches beyond themselves.
now: You worry about your teenager's friends, your marriage after a hard year, the baby who will not sleep. {reward}This is the dua for all of it{/reward}: not just that they are fine, but that they bring joy that reaches the Hereafter.
old: My family will turn out fine if I work hard and provide well.
new: The comfort I really want in my family is a gift I have to ask Allah for.
try: Memorize this dua today and say it for your family after one prayer.

title: The high chamber is theirs because they were patient.
subtitle: Greeted with peace at the end
then: After listing the servants' traits, Allah names the reward: {reward}the high chamber{/reward}, named for its elevation. Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}because of their patience in doing what they did{/idea}. They will be met {reward}with words of welcome, honor, and peace{/reward}.
now: Answering rudeness with calm, waking for night prayer, spending in balance, walking out of the gossip. None of it is flashy. {idea}All of it takes patience.{/idea} That is exactly what the verse says is rewarded.
old: These small efforts do not add up to much.
new: The patience in my small daily efforts is what earns the high place.
try: Choose one trait from verses 63-74 and practice it patiently today.

title: Forever there: a beautiful home and a place to rest.
subtitle: The home they will never want to leave
then: Ibn Kathir says they will {reward}settle there and never leave, move or die{/reward}, and never wish to move elsewhere. The words mirror verse 66: they had asked to be kept from {trap}an evil settlement{/trap}, and they receive {reward}an excellent one{/reward}.
now: You have moved four times in six years. Leases end, rent goes up, jobs change cities. {reward}The verse promises a home you will never have to pack up{/reward}, and never want to.
new: The permanent home is promised, and every patient step points toward it.
try: Next time you feel unsettled about where you live, ask Allah for the home that never ends.

title: My Lord would not care for you, if not for your prayer.
subtitle: The surah ends on what makes us matter
then: The surah closes with a word to the deniers of Makkah. Ibn Kathir says {idea}He would not pay attention to you if you did not worship Him, for He created mankind to worship Him alone{/idea}. Their denial would stay with them. Ibn Mas'ud and others linked it to Badr; Al-Hasan to the Day of Resurrection.
now: You measure your worth by your job title, your follower count, what your family thinks. Some days you feel invisible. {idea}What makes you matter to Allah is that you call on Him.{/idea} Every dua is you being seen.
old: I matter because of what I achieve and who notices.
new: I matter to my Lord because I turn to Him and call on Him.
try: Make one dua today just to talk to Allah, with nothing to ask for but nearness to Him.
